title: Regional driver rollout - evacuation cadence and capacity impact worksheet (July 2026)
body:
Purpose:
This worksheet captures the proposed multi-region cadence for a GPU driver rollout that requires staged evacuation of running inference instances. Goal: complete the driver upgrade with minimal SLA impact, clear rollback/fallback paths, and measurable validation signals.

Scope:
- Regions: us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1, asia-east1
- Fleet segments: dedicated-pool-a, shared-pool-b, preemptible-burst-c
- Driver package: nv-driver-540.14 -> nv-driver-542.08 (kernel ABI change)
- Timebox: July 10–20, 2026 maintenance window nights (region-local nights)

High-level timeline (wave-based):
- Wave 0 (canary): 2 hosts per region, non-critical capacity, full smoke tests (1 hour window)
- Wave 1 (low-impact): 10% of dedicated capacity, rolling with 15m stagger per host
- Wave 2 (medium-impact): 30% of capacity, batch drains with 30m stagger windows
- Wave 3 (bulk): remaining capacity, conservative throttling and extended monitoring

Per-region plan (summary table style lines):
- us-west1 | Window: 2026-07-11 01:00-06:00 PDT | Hosts planned: 120 (24 per wave) | Expected peak impact: 18% token throughput drop at T+15m | Fallback pool: us-west1-burst-reserve (40 GPUs)
- us-east1 | Window: 2026-07-13 00:00-06:00 EDT | Hosts planned: 160 (split across AZs) | Expected peak impact: 20% | Fallback pool: us-east1-secondary-pool (50 GPUs)
- eu-west1 | Window: 2026-07-15 23:00-05:00 CEST | Hosts planned: 80 | Expected peak impact: 22% | Fallback pool: eu-west1-burst (30 GPUs)
- asia-east1 | Window: 2026-07-18 02:00-08:00 CST | Hosts planned: 60 | Expected peak impact: 25% (higher due to tighter spare capacity) | Fallback: route to neighboring region (eu-west1 if latency tolerable)

Selection heuristic for hosts to evacuate (to minimize customer impact):
- Prefer empty or low-utilization hosts (avg token/sec < 5)
- Prefer hosts with <= 10 active sessions and no pinned VIP customers
- Avoid nodes currently running long-latency jobs (batch finisher) or pinned enterprise workloads unless pre-approved
- Prefer hosts in AZs with >= 20% spare capacity post-evacuation

Drain sequencing and eviction policy:
- Initiate graceful drain (SIGTERM to serving process) -> 5m quiet period -> force terminate old sessions if still present after 20m
- Use rolling drain command with concurrency limit: 4 hosts concurrently in Wave 1, increase to 12 hosts concurrently in Wave 3 if metrics stable
- Honor tenant isolation: Dedicated pools first drained within their own capacity class; do NOT mix dedicated and shared drains in the same wave unless explicitly planned

Estimated capacity and unit economics impact (working numbers):
- Expected token/sec reduction per 10% drained capacity: ~9-12% depending on batching efficiency loss
- Cost delta during fallback (using burst reserve): +8% hourly GPU spend during fallback windows
- SLA risk: 99.95% target remains achievable if falls under 15% sustained capacity reduction; above that, we must enable limited fallback routing and rate-limits

Observability and success criteria (queries & thresholds):
- Key metrics to watch (Prometheus/Grafana): 
  - gpu_utilization_pct (per-host) -> should trend down on draining hosts and return to baseline after re-add
  - request_latency_p50/p95 per region -> p95 must not increase > 30% from baseline for >10m
  - queued_requests_count -> must not exceed 2x baseline sustained for >15m
  - token_throughput_region -> compare expected capacity curve, alert if deviation >12%
- Canary success: 0 permanent crash loops, zero core dumps, p95 latency delta < 10%
- Wave success: no customer errors >0.5% and no sustained queued increase beyond threshold

Fallback and rollback options (clear steps):
- Automatic fallback: Smart router will divert up to 20% of routed traffic to fallback pools (configured per-route) when queue depth > threshold
- Manual rollback: If kernel-driver incompatibility observed (GPU OOMs, NVIDIA process crashes), revert host image to previous AMI with nv-driver-540.14 and bring host back into service; estimated time-to-recover per host: 18–35 minutes including image spin-up
- Cross-region overflow: If single-region fallback insufficient, enable overflow routing to paired regions with relaxed latency budgets and degraded throughput SLAs communicated to ops/CS

Communication and run-of-show (templates):
- Slack: #infra-maintenance -> status updates every 15 minutes during waves (format: [region] [wave] [hosts drained]/[total] [p95 delta] [action])
- Status page: Pre-announce 48h before window with expected impact and ETA; update post-canary within 2h of completion
- Customer outreach: Solutions/RM notify top-20 enterprise customers 72h prior if their dedicated workloads are in-scope

Pre-maintenance checklist (owners):
- Infrastructure image baked and validated (Owner: Tomás Ortega)
- Canary test harness updated (Owner: Aisha Raman)
- Fallback pools scaled and smoke-tested (Owner: Liam Chen)
- Runbook and rollback steps reviewed by SRE (Owner: Priya Desai)
- Pager on-call notified and escalation tree reviewed (Owner: Sofia Martinez)
- Backup snapshots for critical nodes completed T-4h

Live runbook excerpts (commands & ops notes):
- drain command: infractl node drain --node $HOST --grace 1200 --force-after 1200
- reimage command: infractl node reimage --node $HOST --image nv-driver-542-rolling-2026-07-10
- health-check: curl -sS http://$HOST:9100/health | jq .status

Validation and post-checks (T+1h, T+24h):
- T+1h: Confirm all drained hosts returned to Ready state and requests servicing normally; snapshot p95/p99 for the window
- T+24h: Run synthetic end-to-end suite covering 90th percentile prompt flows, compare quality/regression signals (reranking/semantic similarity tests)
- T+72h: Finalize incident notes and capacity reconciliation; mark bulk wave as closed in calendar

Risk matrix (short):
- Driver crash on 1 host -> Severity: low; Impact: localized; Remediation: reimage host, collect logs; Owner: on-call
- Driver kernel incompatibility causing core dumps across AZ -> Severity: high; Impact: multi-host outage; Remediation: immediate rollback region, enable cross-region overflow, start incident bridge; Owner: infra lead + SRE
- Unexpected latency spike beyond fallback capacity -> Severity: medium; Impact: customer-visible degradation; Remediation: enable routing rate-limits, spin extra fallback nodes, notify CS

Post-maintenance accounting (what to record):
- Hosts drained vs planned (CSV row per host: host, AZ, start_ts, end_ts, outcome)
- Resource-hours consumed by fallback pools (for cost reconciliation)
- Any customer-facing incidents (Jira links) and remediation timeline

Action items before final sign-off:
- Validate kernel modules on 3 GPU families we run in prod (A100 v1, H100 SXM, A10) (Owner: Aisha Raman)
- Run end-to-end eval with 1000 synthetic prompts on canary hosts (Owner: Tomás Ortega)
- Confirm cross-region routing limits are configured and tested in staging (Owner: Liam Chen)

Appendix - useful links and queries:
- Prometheus queries: avg_over_time(request_latency_p95[10m]) by (region)
- Grafana dashboard: infra/maintenance/driver-rollout-2026-07 (staging link)
- Debug collection command: journalctl -u redwood-serving --since "1 hour ago" > /tmp/serving.log

Notes and open questions:
- Still need sign-off from Product for planned cross-region overflow for eu->us during eu bulk wave (action: Priya to get approvals by 2026-07-05)
- Confirm whether preemptible pools are allowed to be used as fallback for enterprise customers (pending legal approval)

This sheet is intended as the operational source-of-truth for the July rollout. Update the CSV host-table in the drive folder as drains proceed; keep this document versioned and record decision notes inline.
